subtopic: Caring for a sick parent while studying
subtype: Approach: talk to teachers about accommodations [Action]
passage:
I'll tell you what worked for me, beta. When I was twenty-one, my mother had a long illness, and I was drowning in missed lectures. I'm Santosh. I was scared to speak to anyone at the department, because I didn't want to look like someone making excuses.

But one Monday I knocked on Professor Sabina's door. She was the head. I told her plainly what was happening at home, said I'd miss some classes, and asked two things: a little flexibility on deadlines, and a way to get the class notes online.

She listened, then said, "Why didn't you come sooner?" She gave me two extra weeks on one paper and arranged for a classmate to share the notes. It cost me an awkward ten minutes. Not asking would have cost much more.

qa.q: Whose door did Santosh knock on that Monday?
Why was Santosh reluctant to speak to anyone at the department?
qa.a: Santosh was afraid of looking like someone making excuses, so pride and embarrassment held the request back.

qa.q: What turning point in the story changed Santosh's semester, and what could have happened otherwise?
qa.a: Knocking on the door and asking plainly changed things; without it, missed lectures and deadlines would probably have piled up unnoticed.

qa.q: How does Professor Sabina see the request when Santosh finally comes?
qa.a: Professor Sabina listens without judgement, and asking why Santosh did not come sooner suggests she would gladly have helped earlier.

grounding: The student explains the situation to the department head and asks for deadline flexibility and class notes online.
